name: MS-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean of about eighteen points
Incumbent Trent Kelly running with a large cash advantage over Cliff Johnson
Prediction markets price Kelly near 96% to win
model.rationale: This northeast Mississippi seat carries an eighteen-point Republican lean, Kelly is a renominated incumbent with roughly double his challenger's fundraising, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a four percent chance, so the forecast stays firmly in Safe R territory near a seventeen-point Republican margin.
model.watch: A late scandal, a surge of outside spending for Johnson, or an unusually strong Democratic turnout wave could narrow the margin, though an outright flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Trent Kelly, the Republican incumbent, seeks another term in this northeast Mississippi district, which leans about eighteen points Republican. He was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with a clear financial edge, having raised roughly one million dollars and holding more than eight hundred thousand on hand, compared with about five hundred fifty thousand raised by Democratic challenger Cliff Johnson. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public general-election polls are available for the race, and major expert raters have not listed it, treating the seat as safely Republican. Prediction markets give Kelly roughly a ninety-six percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and fundraising advantage points to a comfortable Republican victory, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
